data.description:
Distinct HIO source/Git-file probes and Hosts.Click environment/debug probes received 403/404 responses. No sensitive disclosure or shared actor is established; separate Hosts.Click preview creation succeeded ordinarily.

Two distinct historical sequences, with no common actor inferred:

1. Harvard International Office, June 21, 2026, 17:33:47–17:34:12 UTC: eight requests under /sites/default/modules/custom/hio_statistics/ ask for .info, .module, .install, README, HIOAjax.php.txt, HIOAjax.phps, HIOAjax.php~ and .git/config. Seven saved bodies are branded 404 pages; Git configuration returns a generic 403. Five alternate module paths also return 404. The bare alternate PHP handler and a normal parameterized control each return 500. A public Statistics page and correctly placed chart JavaScript return 200; neither shows server-side source disclosure. A separate April file:///foo parameter test returns 405, with no established parser behavior or connection to June.

2. Hosts.Click, June 21, 2026, 23:24:43–23:24:47 UTC: 17 indexed captures include /.env (403), /_profiler and /_wdt (404), API/documentation guesses and public robots/sitemap requests. The two debug bodies equal the ordinary /api/ missing-route control. Seven responses in this window were inspected; the other window records are index-only evidence. No environment values or debugging access are shown. Generic HIO and Hosts.Click refusal bytes being identical does not connect their requesters.

Separate ordinary context: the June 22 00:07:17 Hosts.Click capture returns 201 with preview_url/subdomain/expires_at. Its original 118-byte body matches the native index SHA-1. An earlier Microlink function result has inner 201 as well. Creation identifiers differ, and neither joins to the two available hosts.li captures. A separately saved World Statistics preview belongs to a different identifier. Creation success is not exploit success, unauthorized access, target-page retrieval through the particular creations, or attribution to the probes. Plain replay of the native creation produced archive 307; an incorrect method-key variant produced archive 404, not target failures.

The ZIP contains 32 saved response bodies with headers/provenance, native row extracts, alternate-path/public controls, both ordinary creation records, the separate preview page, attribution-search records, an offline builder, and original-versus-redacted hashes. All 32 original body hashes/lengths match local saved provenance. Many decoded replay SHA-1 values differ from native CDX payload digests; original compression may explain this, but these are not labeled WARC-digest verified. Redacted output has separate hashes.

The saved historical program-search summary reports 1,937/22/1,959 target-matching rows across three overlapping collections. Its filter code was not preserved. A reproducible broader text-only recheck selects 1,939/30/1,969 rows; both scopes find zero exact sensitive-path probes. All recheck-selected rows and their source line/file hashes are included. Collections overlap and counts must not be added or called actors. Normal statistics, publishing and guest-preview programs do not establish execution of the sensitive probes. No source-IP/session/author/model join is available; SAWP5 is an archive collection label. This is not an exhaustive search of all records or encodings.

This is new characterization within the local review, not proven first public discovery. Neither target is identified as government; AI provider is Unknown. Best tentative category is Other: source/configuration disclosure probing, no success established. Packaging was entirely offline: no live target/archive requests, credential uses, browser rendering, archived code execution, new scans or submissions. Cookies, credentials, preview capabilities and encoded carriers were scrubbed. Archived content is inert text. Credit Laura.
